additional_info.subject: ID0438459-DC/Si-D/RO-[MP / P1 170000128] Left connector not charging CRM:00315002872
additional_info.body:
Hi Traian,
It seems that the problem is still the same. To troubleshoot this problem we would need to go on-site with an EV to make sure to find where the problem is. The issue can only come from either the contactor QA21-22 or in the circuit of the voltage transducer.
If you have crocodile tips for the multimeter, we can measure on the DC busbar and confirm if it's the contactor or not.
The idea is to measure the voltage during the PreCharge and see if it has the voltage we see on the Converters.
If the voltage is not correct according to the converters, then we need to replace the contactors.
If the voltage is correct, the next step is to measure between the XD41:43B and 44D and see if we also get the same voltage (2-10V)
So, if we have a 400V in PreCharge we should measure around 4.1V
If we don't measure that here, then we need to make sure of 2 things:
WC22 and WC23 are not loose (hard to be, but worth to check everything)
This TF1 output to XD41 is also properly attached/cables are ok.
If the voltage is being measured correctly on the XD41, we need to move on to XD10.1.
I don't know if you remember we had this problem before where these orange/green connectors get loose very often and might not have 100% contact to the PLC cartridge and can cause a bad reading.
You can push the connectors together from inside-out (be careful you need to open the converters plate to do this, only with charger powered off)
If it still isn't working we need to measure the 4.1V on the cables input of KF7.
If we don't get 4.1V maybe there is something wrong the cables, otherwise, if we get 4.1V on the input, we need to check the back of the KF7 and see if there are any bended pins or similar that might cause a problem.
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​With these instructions I recommend you to take a spare pair of contactors QA21-22 and TF1. Since this charger is out of warranty feel free to take a KF7 but in my experience I've never replaced a PLC cartridge before, so it is very unlikely.
For the contactors:
https://mall.industry.siemens.com/mall/de/DE/Catalog/Product/?mlfb=%208EM5903-0AA00-7AA8
For the TF1:
https://mall.industry.siemens.com/mall/de/DE/Catalog/Product/?mlfb=%208EM5903-0AA01-0AA5
For the KF7:
https://mall.industry.siemens.com/mall/de/DE/Catalog/Product/?mlfb=%206ES7134-6HD01-0BA1

additional_info.subject: ID0438459-DC/Si-D/RO-[MP / P1 170000128] Left connector not charging CRM:00315003026
additional_info.body:
Hi Traian, good afternoon.
To summarize all the actions performed today:
Checked again TF1 and it is reading properly
Replace QA22 since the measurement from DC+ to DC- was not ok again (not closing)
Checked all the connections to the QA21 and QA22
Checked the nut and WC's tightness
Removed the DC connections from the roof of DC1 to isolate the error and find if it was related to the cable -> not the cable
Checked the FC8.2 and we have no continuity -> broken fuse
Confirmed by swapping DC1 fuse with DC2 and DC1 is now working again. -> Confirmed Fuse problem.
Finally we found the problem. As we aligned, in my honest opinion, we should remove the DC fuse completely in order to avoid further future problems with this component, since it's no longer required as per Phoenix Contact's statement.
Here is the MLFB for the copper bar to replace the fuse:
8EM5901-1AA02-2AA5
https://sieportal.siemens.com/de-de/products-services/detail/%25208EM5901-1AA02-2AA5?tree=CatalogTree
Since we provided a solution, we will close this ticket. If you can please take 1min to fill in the survey as it helps us :)
If you need anything else regarding this topic, please call me or message me on Teams.
Thank you very much for your time and patience. See you on the next ticket.
Best regards,
Francisco
